prompt:
In an experiment to determine the acceleration of free fall g, a steel ball is dropped from different heights h above a pressure sensor trapdoor. The data obtained is plotted on a graph of 2h against t^2.
(a) Explain why the gradient of this graph represents g. [1 mark]
(b) The line of best fit has a gradient of 9.74 m s^-2. Calculate the percentage difference between this experimental value and the standard value of 9.81 m s^-2. [1 mark]
(c) Suggest one reason why a small steel sphere is used rather than a hollow plastic ball of the same size. [1 mark]
hints: For part (a), rearrange h = 0.5 g t^2 to make 2h the subject.
For part (b), use percentage difference = (|experimental - accepted| / accepted) x 100%.
For part (c), compare the relative significance of air resistance for dense vs light objects.
solution:
(a) From h = 0.5 g t^2, multiplying by 2 gives 2h = g t^2. In the form y = m x where y = 2h and x = t^2, the gradient m equals g.
(b) Percentage difference = (|9.74 - 9.81| / 9.81) x 100% = (0.07 / 9.81) x 100% = 0.714%.
(c) A steel sphere has much greater weight relative to air resistance (or higher density), making the effect of air resistance negligible compared to a hollow plastic ball.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: Part (a): Rearrange h = 0.5 g t^2 to 2h = g t^2. Identify gradient of 2h versus t^2 is g [1 mark].
Step 3: Part (c): State that steel ball has higher weight to drag ratio / less affected by air resistance [1 mark].
